title: 人工智能，从零搭建 · 第29部分：智能体与世界

chapters.Fast: 16. 动作词元，以及机器人基础模型

a93b3bdf846b.en: A chatbot answers one question. <bookmark mark='j'/> An agent has to do a whole job: thirty steps, a hundred, a thousand, each depending on the last. <bookmark mark='a'/> Even at ninety-seven percent per step, thirty steps in a row succeed only 40 percent of the time.
a93b3bdf846b.zh: 聊天机器人，回答一个问题就够了。<bookmark mark='j'/>智能体却要完成一整项工作：30步、100步、1000步，每一步都取决于上一步。<bookmark mark='a'/>就算每一步都有97%的把握，连着走30步，也只有40%的时候能全部做对。

b83817c7897d.en: Here are 60 attempts at once. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each step, a few more runs go wrong, and a run that has gone wrong stays wrong. <bookmark mark='b'/> By step thirty, 27 of 60 are still on track.
b83817c7897d.zh: 这里是同时进行的60次尝试。<bookmark mark='a'/>每走一步，就又有几次出了错；而一次尝试一旦出错，就会一直错下去。<bookmark mark='b'/>到了第30步，60次里还有27次走在正轨上。

009833b34f23.en: This is Part 29 of AI, Built: agents and worlds. <bookmark mark='a'/> We start with history, from the first robot that planned to the first cars that drove themselves, and with how to act when you can't see everything. <bookmark mark='r2'/> Then the loop every language-model agent runs, with its tools and memory. <bookmark mark='r3'/> Then long horizons: why errors compound, how fast agents' horizons are growing, and how coding and computer-use agents are measured. <bookmark mark='r4'/> Then imitation, and why copying an expert fails in a way that grows with the square of the task's length. <bookmark mark='r5'/> Then world models, including a small Dreamer trained on this computer, <bookmark mark='r6'/> and finally robots: from simulation to reality, and the models that turn pictures and words into motion.
009833b34f23.zh: 这是《人工智能，从零搭建》的第29部分：智能体与世界。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们从历史讲起：从第一个会做计划的机器人，到第一批自己开车的汽车；还要讲，看不全的时候该怎样行动。<bookmark mark='r2'/>然后是每个语言模型智能体都在运行的那个循环，以及它的工具和记忆。<bookmark mark='r3'/>然后是长时程：为什么误差会累积，智能体的时间跨度增长得有多快，编程智能体和使用电脑的智能体又是怎样被衡量的。<bookmark mark='r4'/>然后是模仿：为什么照搬专家会失败，而且失败的程度随任务长度的平方增长。<bookmark mark='r5'/>然后是世界模型，包括一个在这台电脑上训练的小Dreamer，<bookmark mark='r6'/>最后是机器人：从仿真走向现实，以及把图像和文字变成动作的模型。

140af788d461.en: Chapter one. From Shakey to agents.

809209fd33d9.en: The story of agents starts in a few rooms at the Stanford Research Institute. From 1966 to 1972, Nils Nilsson, Charles Rosen and their colleagues built Shakey, the first mobile robot that reasoned about its own actions. <bookmark mark='a'/> It looked with a television camera, <bookmark mark='b'/> planned in logic, <bookmark mark='c'/> and then moved, so slowly that its name came from how it wobbled. <bookmark mark='d'/> Its by-products outlived it: the A-star search of Part 2, the STRIPS planner, and a better way to find lines in pictures. <bookmark mark='e'/> And it fixed a pattern for decades: sense the world, build a model of it, plan, act, and sense again.
809209fd33d9.zh: 智能体的故事，开始于斯坦福研究所的几个房间。1966年到1972年，尼尔斯·尼尔森、查尔斯·罗森和同事们造出了Shakey，第一个能对自己的行动进行推理的移动机器人。<bookmark mark='a'/>它用一台电视摄像机来看，<bookmark mark='b'/>用逻辑来做计划，<bookmark mark='c'/>然后才动起来，动得那么慢，摇摇晃晃，它的名字就是这么来的。<bookmark mark='d'/>它的副产品比它活得更久：第2部分的A星搜索，STRIPS规划器，还有一种在图像里找直线的更好办法。<bookmark mark='e'/>它还定下了一个延续几十年的模式：感知世界，为它建一个模型，做计划，行动，然后再感知。

2e8364a79c2c.en: The next leap came from the desert. In March 2004, the American defence research agency DARPA offered a million dollars to any robot car that could drive about a hundred and forty miles across the Mojave on its own. <bookmark mark='a'/> None came close: the best, Carnegie Mellon's Sandstorm, went about seven miles and got stuck on an embankment. <bookmark mark='b'/> Eighteen months later, five cars finished a hundred-and-thirty-two-mile course, and Stanford's Stanley won in under seven hours. <bookmark mark='c'/> What made the difference was learning: Stanley taught itself to recognise the road far ahead in its camera images, using what its lasers measured up close as the labels. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 2007 the Urban Challenge put the cars in traffic, among stop signs and other robots; six finished, and Carnegie Mellon's Boss won. The engineers from these races went on to build today's self-driving cars.
2e8364a79c2c.zh: 下一次飞跃，来自沙漠。2004年3月，美国国防部的研究机构DARPA悬赏一百万美元，给任何一辆能自己穿越莫哈韦沙漠、开大约140英里的机器人汽车。<bookmark mark='a'/>没有一辆接近终点：最好的，卡内基梅隆大学的Sandstorm，开了大约7英里，就卡在了一道路堤上。<bookmark mark='b'/>18个月后，有五辆车跑完了132英里的赛道，斯坦福大学的Stanley用不到7个小时夺冠。<bookmark mark='c'/>带来这个差别的，是学习：Stanley用激光雷达在近处测到的结果当作标签，自己学会了在摄像头画面里认出远处的路。<bookmark mark='d'/>2007年的城市挑战赛，让这些车开进车流，周围是停车标志和别的机器人；六辆跑完全程，卡内基梅隆大学的Boss获胜。参加这些比赛的工程师，后来造出了今天的自动驾驶汽车。

423f851ceadf.en: Meanwhile robots began to learn their skills instead of having them programmed. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1989 Dean Pomerleau's ALVINN steered a van along a road with a small neural network that copied a human driver, the idea of chapter nine. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2016 Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn and colleagues trained one network from camera pixels straight to motor torques, and a room of robot arms at Google learned to grasp from hundreds of thousands of attempts. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2019 an OpenAI robot hand solved a Rubik's cube after training only in simulations it never fully trusted. <bookmark mark='d'/> And in 2022 language models began choosing what a robot should do next, while Google's RT-1, a transformer, learned seven hundred tasks from a hundred and thirty thousand demonstrations.
423f851ceadf.zh: 与此同时，机器人开始学习自己的本领，而不再全靠编程。<bookmark mark='a'/>1989年，迪恩·波默洛的ALVINN用一个小小的神经网络，模仿人类司机，驾驶一辆面包车沿着道路行驶，这正是第9章的思路。<bookmark mark='b'/>2016年，谢尔盖·莱文、切尔西·芬恩和同事们训练了一个从摄像头像素直接到电机力矩的网络；同一年，谷歌一屋子的机械臂，从几十万次尝试中学会了抓取。<bookmark mark='c'/>2019年，OpenAI的一只机械手解开了魔方，它只在模拟中训练过，而这些模拟它从来没有完全信任过。<bookmark mark='d'/>2022年，语言模型开始为机器人决定下一步该做什么；而谷歌的RT-1，一个Transformer，从13万次示范中学会了700项任务。

76d5f65dfc6f.en: The newest agents grew out of language models. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2021 OpenAI's WebGPT learned to search the web and quote what it found. In 2022 ReAct had a model alternate between thinking and acting. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2023 models learned to call tools, from calculators to any program described in a few lines of JSON. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2024 agents fixed real bugs in real repositories, and began to use a computer's screen and mouse; <bookmark mark='d'/> by 2025 they wrote code in a terminal for long stretches, and by 2026 for hours on end. <bookmark mark='e'/> Underneath all of it is one loop, older than Shakey: act, see what happened, decide again. The rest of this part is about that loop, in software and in the physical world.
76d5f65dfc6f.zh: 最新的智能体，是从语言模型里长出来的。<bookmark mark='a'/>2021年，OpenAI的WebGPT学会了上网搜索，并引用它找到的内容。2022年，ReAct让模型在思考和行动之间交替。<bookmark mark='b'/>2023年，模型学会了调用工具，从计算器，到任何用几行JSON描述的程序。<bookmark mark='c'/>2024年，智能体在真实的代码库里修复真实的bug，还开始使用电脑的屏幕和鼠标；<bookmark mark='d'/>到2025年，它们能在终端里连续写很长时间的代码，到2026年，能连着干上好几个小时。<bookmark mark='e'/>这一切的底下，是同一个循环，比Shakey还要古老：行动，看看发生了什么，再做决定。这一部分剩下的内容，讲的就是这个循环，在软件里，也在物理世界里。

d26135dcf248.en: Chapter two. Acting without seeing everything.

03abbc06dc95.en: An agent acts in a world it can only partly see. Part 26's Markov decision process assumed the agent sees the state. <bookmark mark='a'/> Drop that, and you get a partially observable Markov decision process, a POMDP. <bookmark mark='b'/> The world still has a state, and moves on when the agent acts. <bookmark mark='c'/> But all the agent gets back is an observation, a clue, drawn from a distribution that depends on the state. <bookmark mark='d'/> Karl Johan Åström showed in 1965 what to do: keep a probability for every state, a belief, and act on that.
03abbc06dc95.zh: 智能体所在的世界，它只能看到一部分。第26部分的马尔可夫决策过程，假定智能体能看到状态。<bookmark mark='a'/>去掉这个假定，就得到部分可观测马尔可夫决策过程，POMDP。<bookmark mark='b'/>世界仍然有一个状态，智能体一行动，它就往前变化。<bookmark mark='c'/>但智能体得到的只是一个观测，一条线索，它服从一个取决于状态的分布。<bookmark mark='d'/>卡尔·约翰·奥斯特伦在1965年指出了该怎么做：给每个状态记一个概率，也就是信念，然后依据信念来行动。

1da29fc00ca8.en: Here's the classic example: a robot in a corridor with a few doors, which doesn't know where it is. Its knowledge is a belief: a probability for every cell, spread evenly at first. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each step it moves right, sometimes slipping, so the belief shifts and blurs. Then it senses: door, or no door, and Bayes' rule from part five multiplies the belief by how well each cell explains what it saw. <bookmark mark='b'/> Watch the uncertainty fall as the pattern of doors gives the place away: from 5.3 bits to 0.8 bits, with its best guess right where the robot is. <bookmark mark='c'/> This is part seven's hidden Markov model, run forward, with the robot's own moves added.
1da29fc00ca8.zh: 这里有一个经典的例子：一条走廊，有几扇门，走廊里有一个机器人，它不知道自己在哪里。它所知道的，是一份信念：每个格子一个概率，一开始平均分布。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一步，它都往右走一格，有时会打滑，于是信念跟着往右挪，也变得更模糊。然后它感知一下：有门，还是没有门；第5部分的贝叶斯法则，把每个格子的信念，乘以这个格子能多好地解释它看到的东西。<bookmark mark='b'/>看，门的排列方式渐渐暴露出它的位置，不确定性也随之下降：从5.3比特降到0.8比特，它最有把握的猜测，正是机器人所在的位置。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是第7部分的隐马尔可夫模型，向前运行，再加上机器人自己的移动。

c1b7d2616541.en: Where did that update come from? The new belief is the probability of each state after the agent's action and the observation it got. <bookmark mark='a'/> Bayes' rule turns it around: how likely the observation is from each state, times how likely the state was before seeing it. <bookmark mark='b'/> And that prior is the old belief pushed through the transitions: the prediction. <bookmark mark='c'/> Together, with eta just making it sum to one: predict, then correct. <bookmark mark='d'/> Strip out the actions, and it is exactly the forward recursion of Part 7's hidden Markov model. With Gaussians in place of tables, it is the Kalman filter that tracks a car on a map.
c1b7d2616541.zh: 这个更新是从哪里来的？新的信念，是智能体做了动作、得到观测之后，每个状态的概率。<bookmark mark='a'/>贝叶斯法则把它倒过来：从每个状态出发看到这个观测的可能性，乘以看到它之前这个状态的可能性。<bookmark mark='b'/>而这个先验，就是旧信念经过状态转移推出来的：预测。<bookmark mark='c'/>合在一起，η只是让它加起来等于1：先预测，再修正。<bookmark mark='d'/>去掉动作，它恰好就是第7部分隐马尔可夫模型的前向递推。把表格换成高斯分布，它就是在地图上追踪一辆汽车的卡尔曼滤波。

ee4fea5fae61.en: The belief is more than bookkeeping. <bookmark mark='a'/> It sums up everything the agent has seen and done: nothing else in the history says more about the present. So a POMDP is an ordinary MDP whose states are beliefs, and Part 26's Bellman equation applies, over a continuum of states. That is why exact POMDPs are so hard to solve, and why the best policy sometimes acts just to learn: walk to a door, to find out where you are. <bookmark mark='b'/> A language-model agent keeps no explicit belief. Its context window plays the part: everything it has read and done so far, from which it must work out what is going on.
ee4fea5fae61.zh: 信念不只是记账。<bookmark mark='a'/>它概括了智能体看到过、做过的一切：历史里再没有别的东西，能对现在说得更多。所以POMDP就是一个普通的MDP，只不过它的状态是信念；第26部分的贝尔曼方程照样适用，只是状态变成了连续的一大片。这就是为什么精确求解POMDP那么难，也是为什么最优策略有时会只为了获得信息而行动：走到一扇门前，弄清楚自己在哪里。<bookmark mark='b'/>语言模型智能体没有显式的信念。扮演这个角色的，是它的上下文窗口：它到目前为止读过、做过的一切，它必须从中推断出眼下是什么情况。

f4abc90543f6.en: A language model only writes text. To make it an agent, put it in a loop. <bookmark mark='a'/> The context starts with a task. The model writes a thought, <bookmark mark='b'/> then an action, in a form a program can read: search for this, run that. <bookmark mark='c'/> The program carries the action out and pastes the result back into the context as an observation. <bookmark mark='d'/> The model reads everything again and writes the next thought and action, until it writes an answer. <bookmark mark='e'/> This pattern, reasoning interleaved with acting, was named ReAct by Shunyu Yao and colleagues in 2022. With one or two worked examples in the prompt, it beat agents trained by imitation and reinforcement learning on two text-based tasks.
f4abc90543f6.zh: 语言模型只会写文字。要把它变成智能体，就把它放进一个循环。<bookmark mark='a'/>上下文从一项任务开始。模型先写下一个想法，<bookmark mark='b'/>再写下一个动作，用程序能读懂的格式：搜索这个，运行那个。<bookmark mark='c'/>程序执行这个动作，把结果作为观测，贴回上下文里。<bookmark mark='d'/>模型把一切重新读一遍，写下一个想法和动作，直到写出答案。<bookmark mark='e'/>这种推理和行动交替进行的模式，是姚顺雨和同事们在2022年命名的，叫ReAct。只在提示里放一两个示例，它就在两个文字任务上，胜过了用模仿学习和强化学习训练出来的智能体。

9db9040e6052.en: Here is a loop running for real, in a small warehouse of our own. The tools are a few functions: list a shelf, look up a price, add. <bookmark mark='a'/> The task: what do three items cost together? The agent's moves come from a script with error rates we chose, not from a language model, so we can count what goes wrong. <bookmark mark='b'/> It looks up a price, reads the observation, keeps a running total. <bookmark mark='c'/> Here it misspells an item 2 times. The tool answers with an error, the error lands in the context, and the agent tries again. <bookmark mark='d'/> Seeing the result of every action is what lets it recover: the answer, 117, is right.
9db9040e6052.zh: 这是一个真正在运行的循环，在我们自己的一个小仓库里。工具就是几个函数：列出一个货架，查一个价格，做加法。<bookmark mark='a'/>任务是：三件东西一共多少钱？智能体的每一步出自一段脚本，错误率由我们设定，而不是来自语言模型，这样我们就能数清楚哪里出了错。<bookmark mark='b'/>它查一个价格，读观测，记下累计的总数。<bookmark mark='c'/>这里它把一个物品的名字拼错了2次。工具回了一个错误，错误进入上下文，智能体就再试一次。<bookmark mark='d'/>能看到每个动作的结果，正是它能纠正过来的原因：答案117，是对的。

86aee6d02eab.en: How does a model learn to use tools at all? <bookmark mark='a'/> In February 2023 Meta's Toolformer taught itself: it tried inserting calls to a calculator or a search engine into ordinary text, and kept the calls whose results made the next words easier to predict. <bookmark mark='b'/> In June 2023 OpenAI made it a product. A program describes each tool to the model with a schema: its name, what it does, its arguments. <bookmark mark='c'/> The model, fine-tuned for this, answers with a structured call instead of prose. <bookmark mark='d'/> The program runs it and hands back the result. Every agent since, coding agents included, is built on this handshake.
86aee6d02eab.zh: 模型到底是怎样学会使用工具的？<bookmark mark='a'/>2023年2月，Meta的Toolformer自学成才：它试着在普通文本里插入对计算器或搜索引擎的调用，保留那些结果能让后面的词更容易预测的调用。<bookmark mark='b'/>2023年6月，OpenAI把它做成了产品。程序用一份模式说明向模型描述每个工具：名字，用途，参数。<bookmark mark='c'/>为此微调过的模型，回答的是一个结构化的调用，而不是一段文字。<bookmark mark='d'/>程序执行调用，把结果交回去。从那以后的每个智能体，包括编程智能体，都建立在这次握手之上。

a132ba256b22.en: Every app that hosts a model needs its tools, and every tool wants to serve every app. <bookmark mark='a'/> Wired up one by one, three apps and four tools take twelve integrations. <bookmark mark='b'/> In November 2024 Anthropic published the Model Context Protocol, MCP: a tool is wrapped once, as a server that lists what it offers, and any app that speaks the protocol can use it. Three plus four instead of three times four. <bookmark mark='c'/> It spread fast. By December 2025 more than ten thousand servers had been published, and the protocol was handed to a new foundation under the Linux Foundation, alongside OpenAI's AGENTS dot md and Block's goose. <bookmark mark='d'/> Google's A2A protocol does the same for agents talking to other agents.
a132ba256b22.zh: 每个装着模型的应用都需要工具，每个工具也都想服务每个应用。<bookmark mark='a'/>一对一地接起来，三个应用和四个工具，就要做12次集成。<bookmark mark='b'/>2024年11月，Anthropic发布了模型上下文协议，MCP：一个工具只需包装一次，做成一个列出自己功能的服务器，任何会说这种协议的应用都能使用它。三加四，而不是三乘四。<bookmark mark='c'/>它传播得很快。到2025年12月，已经发布了一万多个服务器，这个协议也被交给了Linux基金会下属的一个新基金会，和它一起的还有OpenAI的AGENTS.md和Block的goose。<bookmark mark='d'/>谷歌的A2A协议，则为智能体之间的对话做了同样的事。

0357636e5d34.en: Chapter four. Memory, and many agents.
0357636e5d34.zh: 第4章。记忆，以及多个智能体。

27bf86d6de34.en: An agent's working memory is its context window, and it fills up. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every thought, action and observation of the loop adds tokens. A long task produces far more than any window holds. <bookmark mark='b'/> When it is full, something has to go. <bookmark mark='c'/> The simplest fix is to summarize: the agent writes down what it has done and what matters, empties the window, and starts again from the summary. Coding agents do this many times in a long session. <bookmark mark='d'/> Earlier, MemGPT treated memory like an operating system, paging facts in and out of the context; and even windows of a million tokens, from Part 15, have a weakness: models use what sits in the middle of a long context less well than what sits at its ends.
27bf86d6de34.zh: 智能体的工作记忆就是它的上下文窗口，而它会被填满。<bookmark mark='a'/>循环里的每个想法、动作和观测都会增加词元。一项长任务产生的内容，远远超过任何窗口能装下的。<bookmark mark='b'/>满了以后，总得丢掉点什么。<bookmark mark='c'/>最简单的办法是总结：智能体写下它做了什么、什么最重要，清空窗口，再从总结出发重新开始。在一次很长的工作里，编程智能体会这样做很多次。<bookmark mark='d'/>更早的时候，MemGPT像操作系统那样管理记忆，把事实调进调出上下文；而即便是第15部分那种上百万词元的窗口，也有一个弱点：放在长上下文中间的内容，模型用得不如放在两头的好。

54a4371dba2a.en: For memory that outlives the window, agents keep notes outside it. <bookmark mark='a'/> A memory is a short text stored with its embedding, the vectors of Part 24. <bookmark mark='b'/> To recall, the agent embeds a question and fetches the nearest notes back into its context. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2023 Joon Sung Park and colleagues filled a simulated town with twenty-five such characters, each retrieving memories by how recent, how important and how relevant they were. <bookmark mark='d'/> Reflexion stored lessons from failures in words, and read them before trying again. <bookmark mark='e'/> And Voyager, in Minecraft, saved every skill it mastered as a program to call later, and collected three point three times as many unique items as earlier agents. Notes, lessons and skills: three kinds of memory.
54a4371dba2a.zh: 要让记忆比窗口活得更久，智能体就在窗口之外记笔记。<bookmark mark='a'/>一条记忆是一小段文字，连同它的嵌入一起存放，也就是第24部分的那些向量。<bookmark mark='b'/>要回想时，智能体把问题也嵌入，再把最近的几条笔记取回上下文。<bookmark mark='c'/>2023年，朴俊成和同事们让25个这样的角色住进一个模拟的小镇，每个角色按照记忆有多新、多重要、多相关来检索记忆。<bookmark mark='d'/>Reflexion把失败的教训用文字记下来，下次尝试之前先读一遍。<bookmark mark='e'/>而Minecraft里的Voyager，把它掌握的每项技能都存成一段可以以后调用的程序，收集到的独特物品，是以前智能体的3.3倍。笔记、教训和技能：三种记忆。

073c460879d6.en: When one context is not enough, use several. <bookmark mark='a'/> A lead agent plans and hands pieces of the task to subagents, each with a fresh context of its own, <bookmark mark='b'/> and each returns only a short summary, so the lead's window stays clear. <bookmark mark='c'/> Anthropic reported in 2025 that such a team beat a single agent by ninety percent on its own research evaluation. That is the company's measurement, on its own test. It also used about fifteen times the tokens of a chat, and on one public benchmark, the number of tokens spent explained eighty percent of the differences in performance. <bookmark mark='d'/> So much of the gain is simply more computation, spread out. It helps most on broad tasks that split cleanly, like research, <bookmark mark='e'/> and less on tightly coupled ones, like changing one codebase, where every agent needs to know everything.
073c460879d6.zh: 一个上下文不够用，就用几个。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个主智能体负责规划，把任务的各个部分交给子智能体，每个子智能体都有一个全新的、属于自己的上下文，<bookmark mark='b'/>每个都只交回一份简短的总结，这样主智能体的窗口就能保持清爽。<bookmark mark='c'/>Anthropic在2025年报告说，在它自己的研究类评测上，这样一个团队比单个智能体强了90%。这是这家公司在自己的测试上的测量。它用的词元，也大约是一次聊天的15倍；在一个公开的基准上，花掉的词元数，就解释了性能差异的80%。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以，收益的很大一部分，只是更多的计算，分散开来而已。它对那些能干净拆分的宽泛任务最有帮助，比如研究，<bookmark mark='e'/>而对紧密耦合的任务帮助较小，比如修改同一个代码库，那里的每个智能体都需要知道所有的事。

f3ad9af6269e.en: Agents work in long chains of steps: read a page, click, write code, run it, read the error. <bookmark mark='h'/> How many steps a task takes, from start to finish, is its horizon, and every step has to go right. <bookmark mark='a'/> If each step succeeds with probability p, a task of n steps succeeds with p to the n. <bookmark mark='b'/> At ninety percent per step, a ten-step task already fails two times in three. At ninety-nine percent, a hundred-step task succeeds only 37 percent of the time. Small errors compound.
f3ad9af6269e.zh: 智能体干活，靠的是一长串步骤：读一个网页，点一下，写代码，运行，再读报错信息。<bookmark mark='h'/>一个任务从头到尾要走多少步，就是它的时程；而每一步都必须做对。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果每一步成功的概率是p，那么n步的任务，成功的概率就是p的n次方。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一步有90%的把握，10步的任务，就已经是三次里有两次失败。每一步有99%的把握，100步的任务，也只有37%的时候能完成。小错误会层层累积。

cecaaf1f3084.en: Our warehouse agent shows where the reliability comes from. Here is how often it gets the total right, against the number of prices it has to look up. <bookmark mark='a'/> Working in its head, every slip is silent, and by sixty steps it is right only 11 percent of the time. <bookmark mark='b'/> With tools, most errors announce themselves: a malformed call comes back as an error, and the agent simply tries again. Only the silent slips compound: 28 percent at sixty steps. <bookmark mark='c'/> Add a check, reading back what it fetched, and most of the silent slips get caught too: 66 percent, for 1.15 calls a step. <bookmark mark='d'/> The points fall close to curves p to the n, though not always where the error rates predict, since two slips can cancel and retries use up the budget: an error the loop can see is an error it can fix.
cecaaf1f3084.zh: 我们的仓库智能体，展示了可靠性从哪里来。这是它算对总数的比例，横轴是它要查的价格个数。<bookmark mark='a'/>全靠在脑子里算，每个失误都是无声的，到60步时，它只有11%的时候是对的。<bookmark mark='b'/>用上工具，大多数错误会自己暴露出来：一个格式不对的调用，会以错误的形式返回，智能体只要再试一次就行。只有无声的失误会累积：60步时是28%。<bookmark mark='c'/>再加一步检查，把取回的东西读一遍，大多数无声的失误也能被抓住：66%，代价是每一步1.15次调用。<bookmark mark='d'/>这些点落在p的n次方曲线附近，但p并不总是错误率所预言的那个值，因为两次失误可能互相抵消，而重试会消耗步数预算：循环能看见的错误，就是它能改正的错误。

f1d22955db6e.en: Turn it around: how long a task can an agent finish half the time? <bookmark mark='a'/> Set p to the n equal to a half, <bookmark mark='b'/> and take logarithms. <bookmark mark='c'/> When p is close to one, minus log p is almost exactly one minus p, the error rate. <bookmark mark='d'/> So the half-time horizon is about zero point seven divided by the error rate per step: at ninety-nine percent, 69 steps. Halve the errors, and the reachable task length doubles. That is the quantity the next chapter tracks for real models.
f1d22955db6e.zh: 反过来问：一个智能体有一半把握完成的任务，最长能有多长？<bookmark mark='a'/>令p的n次方等于二分之一，<bookmark mark='b'/>再取对数。<bookmark mark='c'/>当p接近1时，负的log p几乎正好等于1减p，也就是错误率。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以，一半把握的时程，大约是0.7除以每一步的错误率：每一步99%的把握，就是69步。错误减半，能完成的任务长度就翻一倍。下一章追踪的，正是真实模型的这个量。

f8160a083757.zh: 第6章。不断翻倍的时间跨度。

e46a86d4bf3b.en: The research group METR turned the length of a task into a measuring stick for agents. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take hundreds of software and research tasks, and time skilled people doing each one: some take seconds, some take a working day. <bookmark mark='b'/> Run an agent on all of them and plot success against the human time, on a log scale. Short tasks it mostly gets, long ones mostly not. <bookmark mark='c'/> Fit a logistic curve, and read off where it crosses one half: the task length the agent finishes half the time, its fifty-percent time horizon. Part 31 looks at how this is measured in detail; here we follow what it shows about agents.
e46a86d4bf3b.zh: 研究机构METR，把任务的长度变成了衡量智能体的一把尺子。<bookmark mark='a'/>拿来几百个软件和研究任务，给熟练的人计时：有的只要几秒，有的要一整个工作日。<bookmark mark='b'/>让一个智能体做所有这些任务，以人的用时为横轴、取对数刻度，画出它的成功率。短任务它大多能做成，长任务大多做不成。<bookmark mark='c'/>拟合一条逻辑斯谛曲线，读出它穿过二分之一的位置：智能体有一半把握完成的任务长度，也就是它的百分之五十时间跨度。第31部分会细讲这是怎么测的；这里我们关注它说明了智能体的什么。

26d14cd1e916.en: Here are METR's measurements: every model they tested, by release date, on a log scale of minutes. <bookmark mark='a'/> GPT-2, in 2019, finished tasks of 3 seconds. GPT-4, in 2023, about 4 minutes. <bookmark mark='b'/> On a log scale the frontier climbs in a straight line, and a straight line on a log scale means a fixed doubling time. <bookmark mark='c'/> Fitting the frontier models since 2023 gives one doubling every 129 days, which is METR's own fit. Over the whole span since 2019, it is 188 days: the pace has quickened. <bookmark mark='d'/> The last frontier model inside METR's reliable range, Claude Opus 4.6, finishes tasks of about 12 hours half the time. By the reasoning of the last chapter, every doubling is a halving of the error per step.
26d14cd1e916.zh: 这是METR的测量结果：他们测过的每一个模型，按发布日期排开，纵轴是取对数的分钟数。<bookmark mark='a'/>2019年的GPT-2，能完成3秒的任务。2023年的GPT-4，大约4分钟。<bookmark mark='b'/>在对数刻度上，前沿模型沿着一条直线上升；而对数刻度上的直线，意味着固定的倍增时间。<bookmark mark='c'/>拟合2023年以来的前沿模型，得到每129天翻一番，和METR自己的拟合一致。从2019年算起的整个时段，则是188天：步伐在加快。<bookmark mark='d'/>还在METR可靠测量范围内的最后一个前沿模型，Claude Opus 4.6，有一半把握完成大约12小时的任务。按照上一章的推理，每翻一番，就是每一步的错误减半。

6c84c3389ca6.en: Half the time is a low bar for work you'd hand over. METR also reports where each model's success curve crosses eighty percent. <bookmark mark='a'/> Those horizons are far shorter. <bookmark mark='b'/> If an agent failed with the same small chance in every minute of work, the compounding of chapter five, the ratio of the two horizons would be fixed: log 2 over log one point two five, 3.1. <bookmark mark='c'/> METR's measurements give a median of 5.1: an agent's success falls off with length more gently than a constant risk per minute would make it. Long tasks are not simply many short ones; some long tasks are easy, and some short ones hard. <bookmark mark='d'/> The eighty-percent horizons are much shorter, but they double at nearly the same pace: every 133 days.
6c84c3389ca6.zh: 对于要托付出去的工作，一半的把握是很低的门槛。METR也报告了每个模型的成功率曲线穿过百分之八十的位置。<bookmark mark='a'/>这些时间跨度要短得多。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果智能体在每一分钟的工作里，都以同样小的概率失败，也就是第5章那种累积，那么两种时间跨度的比值就是固定的：log 2除以log 1.25，等于3.1。<bookmark mark='c'/>METR的测量给出的中位数是5.1：智能体的成功率随长度下降得，比每分钟风险恒定时更平缓。长任务并不只是很多个短任务；有些长任务很容易，有些短任务却很难。<bookmark mark='d'/>百分之八十的时间跨度短得多，但它们翻倍的速度几乎一样：每133天。

eb0fe9410dea.en: The ruler itself is running out. <bookmark mark='a'/> METR says its current tasks cannot reliably measure horizons above sixteen hours. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its last frontier measurement, Claude Mythos Preview (early) in April 2026, came out at about 17 hours, already past that line, and in September 2026 the page stopped being updated. <bookmark mark='c'/> And a horizon on a benchmark is not a job: METR's own trial found experienced developers slower, not faster, with early-2025 tools. Part 31 asks how far such trends can be trusted. Next, how coding agents in particular are measured.
eb0fe9410dea.zh: 这把尺子本身也快用完了。<bookmark mark='a'/>METR说，它现有的任务，没法可靠地测量16小时以上的时间跨度。<bookmark mark='b'/>它最后一次测量前沿模型，是2026年4月的Claude Mythos Preview (early)，结果大约是17小时，已经越过了这条线；2026年9月，这个页面停止了更新。<bookmark mark='c'/>而且，基准上的时间跨度并不等于一份工作：METR自己的对照试验发现，有经验的开发者用上2025年初的工具，速度反而更慢了，而不是更快。这样的趋势能信到什么程度，是第31部分的问题。接下来，看看编程智能体具体是怎样被衡量的。

56dc3312e2ca.en: How do you test a coding agent? In 2023 Carlos Jimenez, John Yang and colleagues at Princeton built SWE-bench from the history of open-source software. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each problem is a real issue reported on GitHub, <bookmark mark='b'/> in a real repository, frozen at the moment before it was fixed. <bookmark mark='c'/> The agent must write a patch. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then the tests the real fix added are run: they must go from failing to passing, while every other test keeps passing. <bookmark mark='e'/> There were 2,294 problems from twelve Python projects. The best model of the day, Claude 2, solved under two percent of them.
56dc3312e2ca.zh: 怎样测试一个编程智能体？2023年，普林斯顿的卡洛斯·希门尼斯、杨约翰和同事们，用开源软件的历史建起了SWE-bench。<bookmark mark='a'/>每道题都是GitHub上真实报告过的一个问题，<bookmark mark='b'/>放在一个真实的代码库里，停在它被修复之前的那一刻。<bookmark mark='c'/>智能体必须写出一个补丁。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后运行真实修复所加的那些测试：它们必须从失败变成通过，同时其他所有测试都要继续通过。<bookmark mark='e'/>一共有2294道题，来自12个Python项目。当时最好的模型，Claude 2，解出的不到百分之二。

1ca24e8d451e.en: The first big gains came from the interface, not the model. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 2024 the same Princeton group gave GPT-4 commands made for it: find a file, look at a hundred lines at a time, edit a range of lines, run the tests. <bookmark mark='b'/> And the environment answers compactly, refusing an edit that would break the syntax. <bookmark mark='c'/> They called it an agent-computer interface, and with the same model it solved twelve and a half percent of SWE-bench, several times more than before. <bookmark mark='d'/> That August OpenAI had developers check every problem in a subset of five hundred, keeping those that were well posed: SWE-bench Verified, the standard yardstick for two years. <bookmark mark='e'/> And by 2025 the loop had moved into developers' own terminals.
1ca24e8d451e.zh: 最早的大进步，来自接口，而不是模型。<bookmark mark='a'/>2024年，同一个普林斯顿团队给GPT-4配了一套为它设计的命令：找文件，一次看一百行，编辑一段行，运行测试。<bookmark mark='b'/>环境的回答也很紧凑，会拒绝会破坏语法的编辑。<bookmark mark='c'/>他们称之为智能体与计算机的接口；用同一个模型，它解出了SWE-bench的12.5%，是以前的好几倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>那年8月，OpenAI请开发者逐题检查了一个500道题的子集，只保留题意清楚的那些：这就是SWE-bench Verified，两年来的标准尺子。<bookmark mark='e'/>到2025年，这个循环已经搬进了开发者自己的终端。

3155bbeb0ad6.en: Then the yardstick wore out. Frontier models came to solve most of Verified, and in February 2026 OpenAI announced it would stop reporting it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Of a hundred and thirty-eight problems its model kept failing, its engineers judged fifty-nine percent to have tests that reject correct fixes. And given nothing but a problem's ID, three frontier models wrote out the real fix, comments included: the answers had leaked into training data. Those are OpenAI's findings. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its suggested successor was Scale AI's SWE-Bench Pro: eighteen hundred and sixty-five problems from forty-one actively maintained repositories, some held back from the public, with bigger changes to make. When it appeared in September 2025, the best models solved about a quarter of it. <bookmark mark='c'/> On Scale's leaderboard today, the top entry, Muse Spark 1.1, solves 61.5 percent of the public set, within a few points of the next.
3155bbeb0ad6.zh: 后来，这把尺子也磨损了。前沿模型能解出Verified的大部分题目，2026年2月，OpenAI宣布不再报告它的成绩。<bookmark mark='a'/>在它的模型一直做不对的138道题里，它的工程师判断有59%的测试会拒绝正确的修复。而且只给题目的编号，三个前沿模型就能写出真实的修复，连注释都一样：答案已经泄漏进了训练数据。这些是OpenAI的结论。<bookmark mark='b'/>它推荐的继任者，是Scale AI的SWE-Bench Pro：1865道题，来自41个仍在积极维护的代码库，其中一些不公开，要做的修改也更大。2025年9月它刚出现时，最好的模型大约能解出四分之一。<bookmark mark='c'/>在Scale今天的排行榜上，排第一的Muse Spark 1.1，解出了公开集的61.5%，和第二名只差几个百分点。

8e22ad5d5c52.en: Real engineering is more than patches. <bookmark mark='a'/> Terminal-Bench, from Stanford and the Laude Institute in 2025, drops an agent into a terminal inside a container with a job to do, like building software, configuring a server or training a model, and a script checks the result at the end. <bookmark mark='b'/> Version 2.0 had eighty-nine such tasks, and frontier agents solved less than two thirds. <bookmark mark='c'/> Benchmarks now get retired as fast as models improve: version 4.0, in 2026, dropped the tasks every model solved and gave each task up to eight hours. <bookmark mark='d'/> In September 2026 Anthropic reported sixty-six percent on it for its newest model: a company's measurement of its own model, to be checked on public leaderboards.
8e22ad5d5c52.zh: 真正的工程不只是打补丁。<bookmark mark='a'/>Terminal-Bench来自斯坦福大学和Laude研究所，2025年推出：它把智能体丢进一个容器里的终端，交给它一项工作，比如构建软件、配置服务器或训练一个模型，最后由一段脚本检查结果。<bookmark mark='b'/>2.0版有89个这样的任务，前沿智能体解出的不到三分之二。<bookmark mark='c'/>如今基准被淘汰的速度，和模型进步一样快：2026年的4.0版，去掉了每个模型都能解出的任务，并给每个任务最多8小时。<bookmark mark='d'/>2026年9月，Anthropic报告它最新的模型在上面得了66%：这是一家公司对自家模型的测量，还要在公开排行榜上核对。

b175873532a4.en: Most software was built for people, with screens and mice, not for programs. So the most general tool an agent can have is a computer of its own. <bookmark mark='a'/> The loop is the same. The observation is a screenshot. <bookmark mark='b'/> The model reads it, as pixels, and answers with an action: click at these coordinates, type this text, press that key. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then it takes another screenshot to see what happened. <bookmark mark='d'/> Anthropic released this as computer use in October 2024, and OpenAI's Operator followed in January 2025. <bookmark mark='e'/> The hardest part turned out to be the most basic: turning what it sees into exactly the right pixel to click.
b175873532a4.zh: 大多数软件是为人设计的，有屏幕，有鼠标，而不是为程序设计的。所以，智能体能拥有的最通用的工具，就是一台属于它自己的电脑。<bookmark mark='a'/>循环还是同一个。观测是一张截图。<bookmark mark='b'/>模型把它当作像素来读，然后回答一个动作：在这些坐标上点击，输入这段文字，按那个键。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后它再截一张图，看看发生了什么。<bookmark mark='d'/>Anthropic在2024年10月以“电脑使用”的名义发布了它，OpenAI的Operator在2025年1月跟进。<bookmark mark='e'/>最难的部分，原来是最基础的那件事：把看到的东西，变成恰好该点的那个像素。

f69e4a6d83f2.en: To measure this, Tianbao Xie and colleagues built OSWorld in 2024: three hundred and sixty-nine real tasks in real desktop apps, from editing a spreadsheet to configuring a mail client, each checked by a script that inspects the machine afterwards. <bookmark mark='a'/> People completed seventy-two percent of them. <bookmark mark='b'/> The best model, at release, twelve. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then the companies reported their own agents: fifteen percent in October 2024, thirty-eight in January 2025, sixty-one by that September. These are the companies' numbers, with their own settings, and the benchmark itself was revised along the way, so read them as a trend.
f69e4a6d83f2.zh: 为了衡量这一点，谢天宝和同事们在2024年建起了OSWorld：369个真实桌面应用里的真实任务，从编辑电子表格到配置邮件客户端，每个任务都由一段脚本在事后检查机器的状态。<bookmark mark='a'/>人能完成其中的72%。<bookmark mark='b'/>发布时最好的模型，12%。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后各家公司报告了自己的智能体：2024年10月15%，2025年1月38%，到那年9月61%。这些是公司自己的数字，用的是它们自己的设置，而且基准本身也一路修订过，所以只能把它们看作一个趋势。

6c05140dfb6c.en: In 2026 the same team released OSWorld 2.0, with tasks of a different size. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each of its hundred and eight workflows takes a skilled person a median of an hour and a half, and an agent around three hundred tool calls, ten times as many as before. On its leaderboard, the best agent finishes one in five outright. <bookmark mark='b'/> Anthropic reports eighty-two percent partial credit for its newest model, on its own runs. <bookmark mark='c'/> Reading the screen brings a new danger. Any web page can contain text written to look like instructions, and the agent reads it with the same eyes it reads its task. <bookmark mark='d'/> An agent that reads untrusted text while holding real permissions is a security problem, one Part 31 returns to.
6c05140dfb6c.zh: 2026年，同一个团队发布了OSWorld 2.0，任务的规模完全不同。<bookmark mark='a'/>它的108个工作流，每个都要熟练的人花上中位数一个半小时，智能体要做大约300次工具调用，是以前的十倍。在它的排行榜上，最好的智能体能完整完成五分之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>Anthropic报告它最新的模型，在自己的运行里拿到了82%的部分得分。<bookmark mark='c'/>读屏幕还带来一种新的危险。任何网页都可能藏着写得像指令的文字，而智能体读它的时候，用的正是读自己任务的同一双眼睛。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个读着不可信的文字、又握有真实权限的智能体，是一个安全问题，第31部分还会回到这里。

87c41bc1e614.en: The simplest way to teach an agent is to show it. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1989 Dean Pomerleau's ALVINN watched the road through a small camera and learned to steer a van by copying a human driver. <bookmark mark='b'/> This is behaviour cloning: record what the expert saw and what it did, and fit a policy by ordinary supervised learning. <bookmark mark='c'/> The average is over the states the expert visits. <bookmark mark='d'/> It is how robot policies start to this day. <bookmark mark='e'/> But there is a catch. Once the learner drives, it visits its own states, not the expert's, and a small mistake takes it somewhere the expert never went.
87c41bc1e614.zh: 教一个智能体，最简单的办法是做给它看。<bookmark mark='a'/>1989年，迪恩·波默洛的ALVINN通过一个小摄像头看路，模仿人类司机，学会了驾驶一辆面包车。<bookmark mark='b'/>这就是行为克隆：记下专家看到了什么、做了什么，再用普通的监督学习拟合一个策略。<bookmark mark='c'/>这里的平均，是对专家到过的那些状态取的。<bookmark mark='d'/>直到今天，机器人策略都是这样起步的。<bookmark mark='e'/>但这里有个陷阱。学习者一旦自己开车，到的就是它自己的状态，而不是专家的；一个小失误，就会把它带到专家从没去过的地方。

4d81654e196c.en: Here is a small driving task we can solve exactly. <bookmark mark='a'/> A car drives up a lane, and each step it can steer left, go straight, or steer right, while a wind keeps pushing it to the right. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every step off the lane costs one. <bookmark mark='c'/> The expert knows exactly where the car is and steers back, so it never leaves the lane. Here are twelve of its drives. <bookmark mark='d'/> The learner sees the road through a camera that is sometimes one cell off. That noise is what makes even a perfect copy make occasional mistakes.
4d81654e196c.zh: 这是一个我们能精确求解的小驾驶任务。<bookmark mark='a'/>一辆车沿着车道往前开，每一步它可以向左打方向、直行或向右打方向，而一阵风一直把它往右推。<bookmark mark='b'/>每离开车道一步，代价是1。<bookmark mark='c'/>专家确切知道车在哪里，会把方向打回来，所以它从不离开车道。这是它的12次驾驶。<bookmark mark='d'/>学习者通过一个摄像头看路，摄像头有时会偏一格。正是这点噪声，让哪怕完美的模仿，也会偶尔犯错。

e5f8e28a6db0.en: Behaviour cloning: give the learner the expert's drives, and for each camera reading it copies the expert's most common action. <bookmark mark='a'/> It only ever saw 5 of the 21 possible readings, the ones near the middle of the road, because those are the only places the expert goes. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now let it drive. Most of the time it copies well: on the expert's own states it chooses differently only 8.5 percent of the time. <bookmark mark='c'/> But one gust at the wrong moment, a misread camera, and it is off the lane, in readings it never saw, <bookmark mark='d'/> and there it has no idea what to do. Of these twelve drives, 5 end off the lane.
e5f8e28a6db0.zh: 行为克隆：把专家的驾驶记录交给学习者，对每一种摄像头读数，它都照搬专家最常用的动作。<bookmark mark='a'/>在21种可能的读数里，它只见过5种，都在路中间附近，因为专家只去那些地方。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在让它自己开。大多数时候它学得很像：在专家自己的状态上，它只有8.5%的时候做出不同的选择。<bookmark mark='c'/>可是一阵风来得不是时候，摄像头读错一次，它就离开了车道，进入它从没见过的读数，<bookmark mark='d'/>在那里它完全不知道该怎么办。这12次驾驶里，有5次最后停在车道之外。

12eeec8f13d2.en: How bad can this get? Let epsilon be the learner's error rate, measured on the states the expert visits: exactly what supervised learning makes small. <bookmark mark='a'/> The chance it has made no mistake in the first t steps is at least one minus the sum of the error rates so far: a union bound. <bookmark mark='b'/> Until its first mistake, the learner is exactly where the expert would be. After it, the worst it can do is pay the full cost every step. <bookmark mark='c'/> Add that up over a task of T steps. <bookmark mark='d'/> Each inner sum is at most T epsilon, so the extra cost is at most T squared epsilon. Stéphane Ross and Drew Bagnell proved this in 2010, and showed tasks where it is reached: twice the horizon, four times the extra cost.
12eeec8f13d2.zh: 这会糟到什么程度？设ε为学习者的错误率，在专家到过的状态上测量：这正是监督学习会把它压小的那个量。<bookmark mark='a'/>前t步一次错都没犯的概率，至少是1减去到目前为止各步错误率之和：这是联合界。<bookmark mark='b'/>在第一次犯错之前，学习者恰好在专家会在的地方。犯错之后，最坏的情况是每一步都付出全部代价。<bookmark mark='c'/>把它在T步的任务上加起来。<bookmark mark='d'/>每个内层的和至多是T乘ε，所以额外的代价至多是T的平方乘ε。斯特凡·罗斯和德鲁·巴格内尔在2010年证明了这一点，还给出了真能达到这个界的任务：时程翻倍，额外代价就变成四倍。

e956707905ae.en: Here is our learner's expected cost, computed exactly, for every horizon up to four hundred steps, over eight seeds. <bookmark mark='a'/> It bends upward: the cost grows faster than the horizon, with a slope of 1.6 on log-log axes, where linear growth would give one. <bookmark mark='b'/> The bound, T squared epsilon, with the measured epsilon of 0.085, is far above it: it is a worst case. If errors simply added up, the cost would follow T epsilon. <bookmark mark='c'/> The reason is on the right: the chance of being off the lane keeps climbing step after step, because a learner that leaves the lane rarely comes back.
e956707905ae.zh: 这是我们的学习者的期望代价，精确算出，时程从1到400步，8个随机种子。<bookmark mark='a'/>它向上弯：代价比时程增长得更快，在双对数坐标上斜率是1.6，而线性增长的斜率是1。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个界，T的平方乘ε，用测得的ε等于0.085，远远高于它：它是最坏情况。如果错误只是简单相加，代价会沿着T乘ε走。<bookmark mark='c'/>原因在右边：离开车道的概率一步接一步地往上爬，因为离开车道的学习者，很少能回来。

efdc8d93c958.en: The cure, from Stéphane Ross, Geoff Gordon and Drew Bagnell in 2011, is to ask the expert about the learner's own mistakes. <bookmark mark='a'/> Let the learner drive. <bookmark mark='b'/> Afterwards, the expert labels every state the learner visited: here is what I would have done. <bookmark mark='c'/> Add those labels to everything collected so far, <bookmark mark='d'/> retrain, and drive again. They called it DAgger, for dataset aggregation. Each round, the data moves towards the states the learner actually reaches, including the ones off the road.
efdc8d93c958.zh: 解药来自斯特凡·罗斯、杰夫·戈登和德鲁·巴格内尔，2011年：就学习者自己的错误去问专家。<bookmark mark='a'/>让学习者开车。<bookmark mark='b'/>事后，专家给学习者到过的每个状态都打上标签：换了我，会这样做。<bookmark mark='c'/>把这些标签加进到目前为止收集的全部数据，<bookmark mark='d'/>重新训练，再开一次。他们把它叫作DAgger，即数据集聚合。每一轮，数据都向学习者真正会到的那些状态移动，包括路外面的那些。

87724a194395.en: Here is DAgger on our lane, round by round. <bookmark mark='a'/> Round one is an expert drive, so the learner knows only the middle of the road. <bookmark mark='b'/> In the next rounds it drives itself, wanders off, and the expert labels the readings it saw out there: steer back. Grey arrows turn into real ones. <bookmark mark='c'/> By round 4 its expected cost over 400 steps has fallen from 345 to 84, and the later rounds keep it there.
87724a194395.zh: 这是DAgger在我们的车道上，一轮一轮的样子。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一轮是专家的一次驾驶，所以学习者只认识路中间。<bookmark mark='b'/>接下来的几轮，它自己开，开出了路，专家就给它在外面看到的读数打上标签：往回打方向。灰色的箭头变成了真正的箭头。<bookmark mark='c'/>到第4轮，它在400步里的期望代价，已经从345降到了84，之后几轮都保持在那里。

ee488a44cf7c.en: Why does this fix the T squared? The trick is to treat the rounds as an online learning game. <bookmark mark='a'/> Now the error that matters is measured on the learner's own states, the ones its own policies visit. <bookmark mark='b'/> Retraining on all the data so far is a no-regret algorithm: on average over the rounds, it does as well as the single best policy in hindsight. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the cost then grows only linearly with the horizon, times u, how much one wrong action can cost later, if the task lets you recover. <bookmark mark='d'/> The difference is where the errors are counted.
ee488a44cf7c.zh: 这为什么能治好T的平方？诀窍是把这些轮次当作一场在线学习的博弈。<bookmark mark='a'/>现在要紧的错误，是在学习者自己的状态上测的，也就是它自己的策略会去的那些状态。<bookmark mark='b'/>每次都在全部数据上重新训练，是一种无悔算法：平均到各轮，它做得和事后看来最好的那个策略一样好。<bookmark mark='c'/>于是代价只随时程线性增长，再乘以u，也就是一个错误的动作以后最多会造成多大代价，前提是任务允许你纠正回来。<bookmark mark='d'/>区别就在于，错误是在哪里被计数的。

14d8eef213b8.en: Now the fair comparison: the same number of expert labels for both, eight seeds each. <bookmark mark='a'/> With the same 400 expert labels, DAgger's cost at 400 steps averages 31 steps off the lane, against 94 for behaviour cloning. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its cost grows more nearly in a straight line, a log-log slope of 1.08 over the first steps against 1.30. The spread across seeds is wide, 67 steps for DAgger, because which readings a learner happens to see matters. <bookmark mark='c'/> More demonstrations barely help behaviour cloning: the expert's drives never leave the lane, so they never show the way back. <bookmark mark='d'/> DAgger keeps improving with labels, to 17 steps at 1600 labels.
14d8eef213b8.zh: 现在做公平的比较：两种方法的专家标签一样多，各用8个随机种子。<bookmark mark='a'/>用同样的400个专家标签，DAgger在400步里平均有31步离开车道，行为克隆则是94步。<bookmark mark='b'/>它的代价更接近直线增长，前几步在双对数坐标上的斜率是1.08，而行为克隆是1.30。不同种子之间的差别很大，DAgger相差67步，因为学习者碰巧看到了哪些读数，影响很大。<bookmark mark='c'/>更多的示范，对行为克隆几乎没有帮助：专家的驾驶从不离开车道，所以从来不会示范怎样回来。<bookmark mark='d'/>DAgger随着标签增多不断改进，到1600个标签时降到17步。

666d62a90432.en: DAgger has a price: an expert on call to label the learner's states. <bookmark mark='a'/> A person cannot easily say, after the fact, how they would have steered at every moment of someone else's drive. <bookmark mark='b'/> So practical versions let the human take over only when the learner goes wrong, and train on the corrections. <bookmark mark='c'/> When the expert is a program, it is easy, and the idea is everywhere: Part 27's on-policy distillation, where the teacher grades the student's own answers, is DAgger for language models. <bookmark mark='d'/> The lesson: learn from where you actually end up.
666d62a90432.zh: DAgger是有代价的：需要一个随叫随到的专家，给学习者的状态打标签。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个人很难事后说清楚，在别人开车的每一刻，自己会怎样打方向。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以实用的版本只在学习者出错时让人接管，再用这些纠正来训练。<bookmark mark='c'/>当专家是一个程序时，这就很容易，而这个思想无处不在：第27部分的在线策略蒸馏，由老师给学生自己的回答打分，就是语言模型版的DAgger。<bookmark mark='d'/>教训是：从你实际到达的地方学习。

f84bd73eedf9.en: An agent that can predict the results of its actions can try things out in its head before doing them. <bookmark mark='a'/> The idea is old. Around 1990 Richard Sutton's Dyna learned a model of the world and practised in it between real steps, and Jürgen Schmidhuber built recurrent networks that modelled their world. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2018 David Ha and Schmidhuber made it vivid. A variational autoencoder squeezes each frame of a game, <bookmark mark='c'/> a recurrent network learns to predict the next squeezed frame, <bookmark mark='d'/> and a tiny controller acts on both. It was the first to score over nine hundred at a car-racing game from pixels, and in VizDoom it was trained entirely inside its own dream. <bookmark mark='e'/> MuZero, in Part 26, went the other way: a model of only what planning needs, never the pixels.
f84bd73eedf9.zh: 一个能预测自己行动后果的智能体，可以在动手之前先在脑子里试一试。<bookmark mark='a'/>这个想法由来已久。1990年前后，理查德·萨顿的Dyna学到一个世界模型，在真实的步骤之间，在模型里练习；于尔根·施密德胡伯也造出了为自己的世界建模的循环网络。<bookmark mark='b'/>2018年，大卫·哈和施密德胡伯把它做得活灵活现。一个变分自编码器压缩游戏的每一帧，<bookmark mark='c'/>一个循环网络学着预测下一帧压缩后的样子，<bookmark mark='d'/>一个很小的控制器根据这两者行动。它第一个在一款赛车游戏里，从像素出发拿到900分以上；而在VizDoom里，它完全是在自己的梦里训练出来的。<bookmark mark='e'/>第26部分的MuZero走了另一条路：只为规划需要的东西建模，从不管像素。

b3cdd81d82c6.en: To plan, an agent needs to predict what its actions will do. A world model learns that from experience. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ours watches a ball bouncing in a box. It squeezes each frame into eight numbers, learns how those numbers change from one frame to the next, and can turn numbers back into a picture.
b3cdd81d82c6.zh: 要做计划，智能体就得预测自己的行动会带来什么。世界模型，就是从经验中学会这一点。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们的世界模型，看的是一个在盒子里弹来弹去的球。它把每一帧压缩成8个数，学会这些数从一帧到下一帧怎样变化，还能把这些数重新变回一幅画面。

d450933417b9.en: How does a world model learn to dream? Here it is at checkpoints during training, each time given the same two opening frames and left to imagine the next twelve, every frame built on its own last guess. <bookmark mark='a'/> Untrained, its brightest pixel is 0.65: a haze, nothing like a ball. <bookmark mark='b'/> After 100 steps its brightest pixel is only 0.08: it has learned the safest guess, a nearly empty frame, the average of all frames. <bookmark mark='c'/> By step 300 it keeps the ball within two pixels of the real one for 5 of the 12 frames, then loses it, as each guess builds on the last one's blur. <bookmark mark='d'/> The final model carries the ball through 12 of the 12 frames, though small errors still add up: after twelve imagined frames, its ball is 1.6 pixels from the real one.
d450933417b9.zh: 世界模型是怎么学会做梦的？这是它在训练途中的几个检查点，每次都给它同样的两帧开头，让它想象接下来的12帧，每一帧都建立在它自己上一个猜测之上。<bookmark mark='a'/>还没训练的时候，它最亮的像素是0.65：一片雾，一点也不像球。<bookmark mark='b'/>训练100步之后，它最亮的像素只有0.08：它学会了最保险的猜法，一张几乎空白的画面，也就是所有画面的平均。<bookmark mark='c'/>到第300步，在12帧里有5帧，它画的球离真实的球不到两个像素，然后就跟丢了，因为每个猜测都建立在上一个猜测的模糊之上。<bookmark mark='d'/>最终的模型，在12帧里有12帧都带着球，不过小误差还是会累积：想象了12帧之后，它画的球离真实的球差1.6个像素。

fe03c75e952b.en: Now let it imagine. Give it two real frames and let it run on its own predictions, step after step, <bookmark mark='a'/> while the real ball keeps going. For a while, imagination and reality move together: one step ahead it's 0.1 pixels off. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then small errors compound, like the long tasks of the last chapter: 4.9 pixels off after twenty steps. <bookmark mark='c'/> Agents like Dreamer learn by practising inside such imagined worlds, and Genie generates whole playable worlds from video.
fe03c75e952b.zh: 现在，让它来想象。给它两帧真实的画面，然后让它靠自己的预测往下走，一步接一步，<bookmark mark='a'/>而真实的球也在继续运动。有一阵子，想象和现实同步前进：往前看一步，只差0.1个像素。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后，小误差开始累积，就像上一章的长任务一样：想象20步之后，差了4.9个像素。<bookmark mark='c'/>像Dreamer这样的智能体，就是在这种想象出来的世界里练习的；而Genie，从视频里生成一个个完整的、可以玩的世界。

174612b754af.en: Chapter twelve. Dreamer: learning inside a dream.

f2d9ed2c50fb.en: Our bouncing-ball model only predicted. Danijar Hafner's Dreamer agents, from 2019 on, learn a world model and then learn to act entirely inside it. Its core is a recurrent state-space model. <bookmark mark='a'/> A recurrent network carries a deterministic memory h from step to step, updated with each action. <bookmark mark='b'/> Beside it sits a stochastic state z, here eight categorical variables. <bookmark mark='c'/> From the memory alone, the prior guesses z without looking at the picture. <bookmark mark='d'/> When there is a picture, the posterior looks at it and corrects the guess. <bookmark mark='e'/> From h and z the model redraws the picture and predicts the reward. <bookmark mark='f'/> DreamerV3, in 2023, ran with one fixed set of settings across more than a hundred and fifty tasks, and was the first to collect diamonds in Minecraft without human data.
f2d9ed2c50fb.zh: 我们那个弹球模型只会预测。达尼亚尔·哈夫纳的Dreamer智能体，从2019年起，先学一个世界模型，然后完全在模型里面学习行动。它的核心是一个循环状态空间模型。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个循环网络带着一份确定性的记忆h，一步一步往下传，每个动作都会更新它。<bookmark mark='b'/>它旁边是一个随机状态z，这里是8个类别变量。<bookmark mark='c'/>只根据记忆，先验在不看画面的情况下猜z。<bookmark mark='d'/>有画面的时候，后验看一眼画面，修正这个猜测。<bookmark mark='e'/>模型从h和z重新画出画面，并预测奖励。<bookmark mark='f'/>2023年的DreamerV3，用同一套固定的设置跑了150多项任务，还第一个在不用人类数据的情况下，在Minecraft里挖到了钻石。

f322597d7634.en: It learns from three terms. <bookmark mark='a'/> Redraw each picture from the state. <bookmark mark='b'/> Predict each reward. <bookmark mark='c'/> And make the prior agree with the posterior, so that the model can predict without looking: that is what lets it dream. The agreement is a KL divergence, and DreamerV2 split it in two. One part, with the posterior frozen, trains the prior towards what was seen. <bookmark mark='d'/> The other, with the prior frozen, nudges the posterior towards states the prior can predict. <bookmark mark='e'/> Weighting the first more, the prior moves more: KL balancing. And below one nat the KL is free, so the posterior is never squeezed to say nothing.
f322597d7634.zh: 它从三项损失里学习。<bookmark mark='a'/>从状态重新画出每幅画面。<bookmark mark='b'/>预测每个奖励。<bookmark mark='c'/>再让先验和后验一致，这样模型不看画面也能预测：正是这一点让它能做梦。这种一致用KL散度来衡量，DreamerV2把它拆成了两半。一半冻结后验，把先验往看到的东西上拉。<bookmark mark='d'/>另一半冻结先验，把后验轻轻推向先验能预测的状态。<bookmark mark='e'/>给前一半更大的权重，先验就动得更多：这就是KL平衡。而KL低于1奈特的部分不计代价，所以后验永远不会被压得什么都不说。

020712ba0c17.en: Does balancing matter? We trained just the world model of our small game both ways, three seeds each, with the same total weight on the KL, <bookmark mark='a'/> and let each dream thirty steps ahead from six real frames, counting the pixels it gets wrong. <bookmark mark='b'/> On a world this small the difference is slight: 5.8 wrong pixels a frame with balancing, 5.6 without. Balancing matters more on harder worlds, like Atari's.
020712ba0c17.zh: 平衡真的重要吗？我们只训练了这个小游戏的世界模型，两种方式各3个随机种子，KL的总权重相同，<bookmark mark='a'/>让每个模型从6帧真实画面出发，往后梦30步，数一数它画错了多少像素。<bookmark mark='b'/>在这么小的世界里，差别很小：用了平衡每帧错5.8个像素，不用是5.6个。在更难的世界里，比如雅达利游戏，平衡更重要。

7431922b0761.en: A second trick from DreamerV3 lets one set of settings work everywhere. Rewards in one game are around one, in another around a thousand, and a squared error is dominated by the largest. <bookmark mark='a'/> So V3 predicts the symmetric logarithm of the reward and undoes it afterwards: close to the identity near zero, logarithmic far away. <bookmark mark='b'/> We trained one small network to predict the rewards of four games whose scales differ a thousandfold. <bookmark mark='c'/> Trained on raw rewards, the network spends itself on the largest game and gets the smallest one 278 percent wrong. With symlog, every game is learned: 2 percent on the smallest, 1 on the largest. Our Dreamer predicts its rewards this way, as a distribution over bins in symlog space.
7431922b0761.zh: DreamerV3的第二个诀窍，让同一套设置在哪里都能用。一个游戏的奖励在1左右，另一个在1000左右，而平方误差由最大的那个主导。<bookmark mark='a'/>所以V3预测的是奖励的对称对数，事后再还原：在0附近几乎就是恒等函数，离得远时是对数。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们训练了一个小网络，去预测四个游戏的奖励，它们的尺度相差一千倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>用原始奖励训练，网络把力气都花在最大的那个游戏上，最小的那个错了278%。用了symlog，每个游戏都学到了：最小的错2%，最大的错1%。我们的Dreamer就是这样预测奖励的，在symlog空间里，表示成一组区间上的分布。

69c0f9f835cc.en: Then the agent learns to act without touching the real game. <bookmark mark='a'/> From states the model has seen, it dreams 15 steps ahead, choosing actions with the current policy, rewards predicted by the model. <bookmark mark='b'/> The return of each dream mixes the rewards it dreamed with a critic's estimate of what comes after, a lambda-return. The policy follows Part 26's REINFORCE, with the critic as baseline, scaled by the spread of the returns, plus a little entropy. <bookmark mark='c'/> The critic learns the dreamed returns. The real game is only used to collect more experience for the model.
69c0f9f835cc.zh: 然后，智能体在不碰真实游戏的情况下学习行动。<bookmark mark='a'/>从模型见过的状态出发，它往后梦15步，用当前的策略选动作，奖励由模型预测。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个梦的回报，把梦到的奖励和评论家对之后的估计混在一起，也就是λ回报。策略按第26部分的REINFORCE来学，用评论家做基线，按回报的跨度缩放，再加一点熵。<bookmark mark='c'/>评论家学习梦里的回报。真实的游戏，只用来给模型收集更多经验。

6344b6b60362.en: Here is our Dreamer-lite learning the game of catch. At each checkpoint it watches the same six real frames, then dreams on, given the same actions as reality. <bookmark mark='a'/> Untrained, its dreams have nothing to do with the game. <bookmark mark='b'/> As it trains, the dreams come to match reality, from 69.5 wrong pixels a frame untrained to 1.8 after 2,400 updates, in pictures with about 7 lit pixels. <bookmark mark='c'/> Errors still creep in the longer it dreams, as in chapter eleven, and a new ball, which appears at a random place, can never be dreamed exactly.
6344b6b60362.zh: 这是我们的迷你Dreamer在学接球游戏。在每个检查点，它看同样的6帧真实画面，然后在同样的动作下继续往后梦。<bookmark mark='a'/>还没训练时，它的梦和这个游戏毫无关系。<bookmark mark='b'/>随着训练，梦越来越接近现实，从未训练时每帧错69.5个像素，降到2400次更新后的1.8个，而每幅画面大约只有7个亮像素。<bookmark mark='c'/>梦得越久，误差还是会慢慢渗进来，就像第11章那样；而新出现的球位置是随机的，永远不可能被准确梦到。

c4dc03d0d5d1.en: And the policy, trained only in those dreams, is tested in the real game. <bookmark mark='a'/> After about 4,556 steps of real play, the 3 seeds catch 100 to 100 percent of the balls, against 29 percent for a random paddle: the policy was learned entirely in dreams. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the right, one of its real games at the end: the paddle heads for where each ball will land, and catches 0 of 0.
c4dc03d0d5d1.zh: 而这个只在梦里训练过的策略，被拿到真实的游戏里测试。<bookmark mark='a'/>在大约4556步真实游戏之后，3个种子接住了100%到100%的球，而随机移动的挡板是29%：这个策略完全是在梦里学会的。<bookmark mark='b'/>右边是它最后玩的一局真实游戏：挡板朝着每个球将要落下的地方移动，0个球接住了0个。

96cf5e5e80c3.en: Chapter thirteen. Worlds you can walk through.
96cf5e5e80c3.zh: 第13章。可以走进去的世界。

4165faad60cd.en: Our world models learned from frames paired with the actions that caused them. The Internet is full of video, but almost none of it records which buttons were pressed. <bookmark mark='a'/> Genie, from Google DeepMind in 2024, learned the actions too. A latent action model looks at two consecutive frames and must explain the change with one of just eight codes, <bookmark mark='b'/> as if guessing which button was pressed. <bookmark mark='c'/> A dynamics model learns to draw the next frame from the past frames and a code. <bookmark mark='d'/> At play time a person picks the codes, and a video model becomes a game you can steer, learned from game videos with no labels at all.
4165faad60cd.zh: 我们的世界模型，是从配好了动作的画面里学的。网上到处都是视频，可几乎没有哪段视频记下了按的是哪个键。<bookmark mark='a'/>谷歌DeepMind在2024年推出的Genie，连动作也一起学了。一个潜在动作模型看相邻的两帧画面，必须只用8个代码中的一个来解释它们的变化，<bookmark mark='b'/>就像在猜按下了哪个键。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个动力学模型，学着根据过去的画面和一个代码画出下一帧。<bookmark mark='d'/>玩的时候，由人来选代码，视频模型就变成了一个可以操控的游戏，而它是从完全没有标签的游戏视频里学出来的。

bfb8f05c759c.en: Then the worlds grew. <bookmark mark='a'/> Genie 2, in December 2024, made three-dimensional worlds from a single picture. <bookmark mark='b'/> Genie 3, in August 2025, drew them at seven hundred and twenty lines, twenty-four frames a second, in real time, and kept them consistent for a few minutes: walk away from a wall and come back, and what you painted on it is still there. Text could change the world as you went, and DeepMind used it to train its SIMA agent. <bookmark mark='c'/> In January 2026 a prototype opened to some subscribers. <bookmark mark='d'/> And on the twenty-seventh of October 2026, DeepMind announced Genie 4, with sound generated alongside the picture and pitched as a place to train robots; by DeepMind's own account, objects can still drift over long sessions.
bfb8f05c759c.zh: 然后，世界变大了。<bookmark mark='a'/>2024年12月的Genie 2，从一张图片生成三维世界。<bookmark mark='b'/>2025年8月的Genie 3，以720p、每秒24帧的画面实时绘制世界，并让它在几分钟里保持一致：从一面墙前走开，再走回来，你在墙上画的东西还在。文字可以边走边改变世界，DeepMind还用它训练了自己的SIMA智能体。<bookmark mark='c'/>2026年1月，一个原型向部分订阅用户开放。<bookmark mark='d'/>而在2026年10月27日，DeepMind发布了Genie 4，声音和画面一起生成，并被定位为训练机器人的场所；按DeepMind自己的说法，在长时间的会话里，物体仍然会漂移。

2ab359e15a71.en: Danijar Hafner's Dreamer line, the subject of the last chapter, reached the same scale. <bookmark mark='a'/> Dreamer 4, in 2025, learned a world model mostly from Minecraft videos, only a small part of them labelled with actions, <bookmark mark='b'/> then trained an agent entirely inside it, <bookmark mark='c'/> and that agent collected diamonds, a task of more than twenty thousand mouse and keyboard actions, without ever playing the real game during training.
2ab359e15a71.zh: 达尼亚尔·哈夫纳的Dreamer系列，也就是上一章的主题，也达到了同样的规模。<bookmark mark='a'/>2025年的Dreamer 4，主要从Minecraft的视频里学到一个世界模型，其中只有一小部分标注了动作，<bookmark mark='b'/>然后完全在模型里训练一个智能体，<bookmark mark='c'/>而这个智能体挖到了钻石，这项任务需要两万多个鼠标和键盘动作，它在训练中却从没玩过真正的游戏。

3586a6de3e86.en: All of these predict pixels: every leaf and every ripple, most of which an agent doesn't need. <bookmark mark='a'/> Part 24's joint-embedding predictive architectures predict an embedding instead, only what the encoder finds worth predicting. <bookmark mark='b'/> Meta's V-JEPA 2 turned this into a world model for a robot. After pretraining on a million hours of video, sixty-two hours of robot video taught it how the arm's actions change what it sees. <bookmark mark='c'/> To act, it imagines many action sequences in embedding space <bookmark mark='d'/> and carries out the one whose predicted embedding comes closest to a picture of the goal. With that, it picked up and placed objects in labs it had never seen. Planning with a learned model, as in MuZero, but the model is learned from video.
3586a6de3e86.zh: 这些模型预测的都是像素：每一片树叶，每一道涟漪，其中大部分是智能体用不着的。<bookmark mark='a'/>第24部分的联合嵌入预测架构，预测的则是嵌入，只预测编码器认为值得预测的东西。<bookmark mark='b'/>Meta的V-JEPA 2把它变成了机器人的世界模型。在一百万小时的视频上预训练之后，62小时的机器人视频教会了它：机械臂的动作会怎样改变它看到的东西。<bookmark mark='c'/>要行动时，它在嵌入空间里想象许多动作序列，<bookmark mark='d'/>执行预测出的嵌入最接近目标图片的那一个。靠这个办法，它在从没见过的实验室里拿起并放下了物体。这是用学到的模型做规划，和MuZero一样，只不过这个模型是从视频里学来的。

0d65277c4f7a.en: Chapter fourteen. From simulation to reality.

9654fd29bc05.en: Robots learn slowly in the real world: one robot, one attempt at a time, wearing out and falling over. So most robot learning starts in simulation. <bookmark mark='a'/> A simulator can run thousands of robots at once, faster than real time, with nothing to break and the true state always known. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2021 and 2022 NVIDIA's Isaac Gym ran thousands of legged robots in parallel on one graphics card, and taught them to walk in minutes. <bookmark mark='c'/> The catch is the reality gap. The simulator's physics are written by people, and wrong in small ways: friction, masses, motor strength, the delay between sensing and acting, the noise in every sensor. A policy that exploits the simulator's quirks fails on the real machine.
9654fd29bc05.zh: 机器人在真实世界里学得很慢：一台机器人，一次一次地尝试，会磨损，会摔倒。所以大多数机器人学习都从仿真开始。<bookmark mark='a'/>仿真器可以同时运行几千台机器人，比真实时间还快，没有东西会坏，真实状态也永远知道。<bookmark mark='b'/>2021年和2022年，英伟达的Isaac Gym在一块显卡上并行运行了几千台腿足机器人，几分钟就教会了它们走路。<bookmark mark='c'/>问题在于现实差距。仿真器的物理是人写的，在很多小地方都不对：摩擦，质量，电机的力量，从感知到行动的延迟，每个传感器的噪声。一个利用了仿真器怪癖的策略，到了真实的机器上就会失败。

51c3215a20f6.en: The fix is counterintuitive: make the simulator worse on purpose. <bookmark mark='a'/> Don't train in one simulator. Train in many, each with its own settings, drawn afresh every episode: different masses, different friction, a slower motor, a delay. <bookmark mark='b'/> A policy that works across all of them cannot rely on any one simulator's quirks, and if the real world looks like just one more draw, it works there too. <bookmark mark='c'/> Josh Tobin and colleagues did this for pictures in 2017, randomizing textures and lights, Xue Bin Peng and colleagues for physics in 2018, and OpenAI's robot hand solved a Rubik's cube in 2019 with randomization that widened itself as the hand improved.
51c3215a20f6.zh: 解决办法有违直觉：故意把仿真器弄得更糟。<bookmark mark='a'/>不要只在一个仿真器里训练。要在很多个里训练，每个都有自己的设置，每个回合重新抽取：不同的质量，不同的摩擦，更慢的电机，一点延迟。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个在所有这些仿真器里都管用的策略，就没法依赖任何一个仿真器的怪癖；如果真实世界看起来只是又一次抽样，它在那里也能管用。<bookmark mark='c'/>2017年，乔希·托宾和同事们对图像这样做，随机化纹理和光照；2018年，彭学斌和同事们对物理这样做；2019年，OpenAI的机械手解开了魔方，用的随机化会随着机械手的进步自己扩大范围。

ded146fc7856.en: Let's try it on Part 26's cart-pole. <bookmark mark='a'/> Our real cart-pole is a different machine: a longer, heavier pole, a weaker motor, a one-step delay, and noisy sensors, all inside the range we randomize over. <bookmark mark='b'/> We train simple linear policies with the cross-entropy method, eight seeds each, with the same number of training episodes, and test every round on the real machine. <bookmark mark='c'/> In Part 26's simulator, both kinds learn to balance for the full five hundred steps. <bookmark mark='d'/> On the real one, the policies trained in a single simulator last 97 steps on average; those trained across randomized simulators, 473.
ded146fc7856.zh: 我们在第26部分的倒立摆上试一试。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们的“真实”倒立摆是另一台机器：杆更长、更重，电机更弱，动作晚一步，传感器有噪声，这些都在我们随机化的范围之内。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们用交叉熵方法训练简单的线性策略，每种方法8个随机种子，训练回合数相同，每一轮都在真实的机器上测试。<bookmark mark='c'/>在第26部分的仿真器里，两种策略都学会了平衡满500步。<bookmark mark='d'/>到了真实的倒立摆上，只在一个仿真器里训练的策略，平均坚持97步；在随机化的仿真器里训练的，坚持473步。

54f4e354e32f.en: Here is the whole picture: how long each kind of policy balances, across pole lengths and motor strengths, every one with the real robot's delay and noise. <bookmark mark='a'/> The policies trained in one simulator balance for four hundred steps nowhere on this map, once the delay and the noise are added. <bookmark mark='b'/> Those trained across randomized simulators, in 83 percent, the real robot included. <bookmark mark='c'/> The price is a policy that is less tuned to any one machine; the gain is that it does not need to know which machine it is on.
54f4e354e32f.zh: 这是全貌：两种策略在不同的杆长和电机力量下能平衡多久，每一处都带着真实机器人的延迟和噪声。<bookmark mark='a'/>只在一个仿真器里训练的策略，一旦加上延迟和噪声，在这张图上没有一处能平衡到400步。<bookmark mark='b'/>在随机化仿真器里训练的，是83%，真实的机器人也包括在内。<bookmark mark='c'/>代价是，策略对任何一台机器都没那么精调；好处是，它不需要知道自己在哪台机器上。

1743d5df5e2d.en: Domain randomization is now routine. <bookmark mark='a'/> Walking and running for legged robots and humanoids are mostly trained this way, in randomized simulation, and moved to the real machine unchanged. <bookmark mark='b'/> In a typical episode on the real cart-pole, the single-simulator policy drops the pole after 43 steps, and the randomized one after 419. <bookmark mark='c'/> The newest step closes the loop with the previous chapters: in October 2026 Google reported building a simulated twin of a real table from a single photo, and DeepMind pitched Genie 4 as a training ground for robots. Simulators that no one writes by hand, only learned.
1743d5df5e2d.zh: 域随机化如今已是常规做法。<bookmark mark='a'/>腿足机器人和人形机器人的走和跑，大多就是这样训练的：在随机化的仿真里训练，再原封不动地搬到真实的机器上。<bookmark mark='b'/>在真实倒立摆上一个典型的回合里，单一仿真器的策略在43步后让杆倒下了，随机化的策略则在419步后倒下。<bookmark mark='c'/>最新的一步，和前面几章连成了一个圈：2026年10月，谷歌报告说，只用一张照片就为一张真实的桌子建起了仿真的孪生体，而DeepMind把Genie 4定位为机器人的训练场。仿真器不再由人手写，而是学出来的。

0ce3618e867c.zh: 第15章。视觉–语言–动作模型。

3ab6fd82c802.en: In chapter one we left robot learning at Google's RT-1, a transformer trained on a hundred and thirty thousand demonstrations. <bookmark mark='a'/> The next step was to borrow a mind. RT-2, in 2023, took a vision-language model trained on the web and fine-tuned it to write the robot's actions as if they were words. On objects and scenes it had never seen, it succeeded sixty-two percent of the time, against RT-1's thirty-two: knowledge from the web, turned into motion. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then twenty-one labs pooled over a million trajectories from twenty-two kinds of robot, the Open X-Embodiment dataset. <bookmark mark='c'/> On it, OpenVLA, with open weights and seven billion parameters, beat the fifty-five-billion-parameter RT-2-X by sixteen and a half points across twenty-nine tasks.
3ab6fd82c802.zh: 在第1章里，我们讲到谷歌的RT-1就停下了，那是一个在13万次示范上训练的Transformer。<bookmark mark='a'/>下一步，是借一个头脑来用。2023年的RT-2，拿来一个在网络上训练好的视觉–语言模型，把它微调成像写字一样写出机器人的动作。在从没见过的物体和场景上，它有62%的时候成功，而RT-1只有32%：来自网络的知识，变成了动作。<bookmark mark='b'/>接着，21个实验室汇集了来自22种机器人的一百多万条轨迹，这就是Open X-Embodiment数据集。<bookmark mark='c'/>在它上面训练的OpenVLA，权重开放，有70亿参数，在29项任务上，比550亿参数的RT-2-X高出16.5个百分点。

2dcd9fdda40e.en: Here is what is inside a vision-language-action model. It starts from a model that already reads images and text, trained on the web. <bookmark mark='a'/> Give it camera images and an instruction, and add a way to output motion. <bookmark mark='r'/> RT-2, in 2023, wrote actions as tokens, like words. <bookmark mark='b'/> Pi-zero, in 2024, added an action expert: a small extra network attached to the vision-language model, whose only job is to output smooth arm motions. It's not one of part sixteen's mixture-of-experts experts. It generates those motions by flow matching, part twenty-one's machinery, now drawing trajectories instead of pictures.
2dcd9fdda40e.zh: 这是视觉–语言–动作模型的内部。它的起点，是一个已经能读懂图像和文字的模型，在网络数据上训练出来的。<bookmark mark='a'/>给它摄像头拍到的画面和一条指令，再给它加上一种输出动作的办法。<bookmark mark='r'/>2023年的RT-2，把动作写成词元，就像写词一样。<bookmark mark='b'/>2024年的π0，加上了一个动作专家：这是挂在视觉–语言模型旁边的一个额外的小网络，它唯一的任务，就是输出平滑的机械臂动作。它可不是第16部分混合专家模型里的那种专家。它用流匹配来生成这些动作；这正是第21部分的那套机制，只不过现在画出来的不是图像，而是运动轨迹。

c299bb7bad5b.en: Here is pi zero's action expert, exactly. <bookmark mark='a'/> A chunk is the next fifty actions, one second of motion. Training draws a straight line from pure noise to the true chunk, <bookmark mark='b'/> and teaches the network the velocity along that line, given what the robot sees: part twenty-one's flow matching. <bookmark mark='c'/> To act, it starts from noise and takes ten small steps along the learned velocity, and the noise becomes a motion.
c299bb7bad5b.zh: 这是π0动作专家的确切形式。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个动作块，是接下来的50个动作，也就是1秒钟的运动。训练时，从纯噪声到真实的动作块画一条直线，<bookmark mark='b'/>让网络在看到机器人眼前画面的条件下，学习沿着这条直线的速度：这就是第21部分的流匹配。<bookmark mark='c'/>行动时，它从噪声出发，沿着学到的速度走10小步，噪声就变成了一段动作。

9434ff7ef654.en: Why go to the trouble of a generative model for actions? Because people demonstrate in more than one way. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here, demonstrations pass an obstacle above or below, half and half. <bookmark mark='b'/> Trained to minimize squared error, the policy learns the average of the two ways round, and the average goes straight through the obstacle: it hits it 98 percent of the time. <bookmark mark='c'/> The flow-matching policy samples one way or the other, above 51 percent of the time and below 49, and hits it 27 percent of the time. Real demonstrations are full of such choices: which hand, which grasp, which way round.
9434ff7ef654.zh: 为什么要费劲给动作用一个生成模型？因为人做示范的方式不止一种。<bookmark mark='a'/>在这里，示范从障碍物的上方或下方绕过，各占一半。<bookmark mark='b'/>以最小化平方误差为目标训练，策略学到的是两条路的平均，而平均正好穿过障碍物：它有98%的时候撞上障碍。<bookmark mark='c'/>流匹配策略则会采样其中一条路，51%的时候从上方绕，49%的时候从下方绕，撞上障碍的比例是27%。真实的示范里，到处都是这样的选择：用哪只手，怎么抓，从哪边绕。

4fe1507d7c70.en: And it doesn't act one tiny step at a time. It plans a chunk of motion, a second or so, then looks at the world again and plans the next: <bookmark mark='a'/> the belief and the world model of the earlier chapters, folded into one network that sees, thinks and moves.
4fe1507d7c70.zh: 而且，它并不是一小步一小步地行动。它一次规划一段动作，大约1秒，然后再看一眼世界，规划下一段：<bookmark mark='a'/>前面几章的信念和世界模型，都合进了同一个网络，它能看、能想、能动。

e8d04028f6e3.en: Chapter sixteen. Action tokens, and robot foundation models.
e8d04028f6e3.zh: 第16章。动作词元，以及机器人基础模型。

fc819f1dc264.en: RT-2 and OpenVLA wrote actions as tokens the simplest way. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take each joint's position at each time step, and round it to one of two hundred and fifty-six bins. <bookmark mark='b'/> For a seven-joint arm at fifty steps a second, that is 350 tokens for one second of motion. <bookmark mark='c'/> And they are nearly all the same: on our smooth test motions, 46 percent of tokens equal the one before, and 75 percent are within one bin of it. <bookmark mark='d'/> A model trained to predict the next token learns mostly to copy, and the information it needs is spread thin across hundreds of tokens.
fc819f1dc264.zh: RT-2和OpenVLA用最简单的办法把动作写成词元。<bookmark mark='a'/>取每个关节在每个时间步的位置，把它取整到256个区间中的一个。<bookmark mark='b'/>对一个7关节、每秒50步的机械臂来说，一秒钟的动作就是350个词元。<bookmark mark='c'/>而它们几乎都一样：在我们平滑的测试动作上，46%的词元和前一个相同，75%和前一个相差不超过一个区间。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个被训练去预测下一个词元的模型，学到的主要是照抄，而它需要的信息，被稀稀拉拉地摊在几百个词元上。

9de62688771f.en: In January 2025 Karl Pertsch and colleagues at Physical Intelligence compressed first. <bookmark mark='a'/> Any smooth motion is a sum of cosine waves, slow ones first, and the discrete cosine transform, the one inside JPEG, lists how much of each wave you need. <bookmark mark='b'/> Smooth motion lives in the slowest few: over our motions, the first three waves carry 99.7 percent of the energy. <bookmark mark='c'/> FAST scales the coefficients, rounds them to integers, so that on this chunk only 4 of 50 are not zero, and lets byte-pair encoding, from Part 23, merge the common patterns into tokens.
9de62688771f.zh: 2025年1月，Physical Intelligence的卡尔·佩尔奇和同事们先做压缩。<bookmark mark='a'/>任何平滑的动作，都是一些余弦波的叠加，慢的波排在前面；离散余弦变换，也就是JPEG里用的那一种，列出每个波各需要多少。<bookmark mark='b'/>平滑的动作，就住在最慢的那几个波里：在我们的动作上，前三个波承载了99.7%的能量。<bookmark mark='c'/>FAST把系数放大、取整成整数，于是在这一块动作上，50个数里只有4个不是零；再让第23部分的字节对编码，把常见的模式合并成词元。

a87d76d32ddc.en: How much does it save? Here is FAST on held-out motions, for a range of scales gamma: tokens per second against the error of the motion rebuilt from them. <bookmark mark='a'/> A bigger gamma keeps more detail and costs more tokens. <bookmark mark='b'/> Per-step binning sits far to the right: 350 tokens. <bookmark mark='c'/> At about the same error, FAST needs 63, 6 times fewer, and each one carries real information. <bookmark mark='d'/> Physical Intelligence reported that a policy writing FAST tokens matched their flow-matching pi zero on many tasks and trained about five times faster.
a87d76d32ddc.zh: 它能省多少？这是FAST在留出的动作上的表现，对一系列缩放系数γ：横轴是每秒的词元数，纵轴是用它们重建出的动作的误差。<bookmark mark='a'/>γ越大，保留的细节越多，花的词元也越多。<bookmark mark='b'/>逐步分箱的做法远在右边：350个词元。<bookmark mark='c'/>在差不多的误差下，FAST只需要63个，少了6倍，而且每一个都带着真正的信息。<bookmark mark='d'/>Physical Intelligence报告说，一个写FAST词元的策略，在许多任务上和他们用流匹配的π0一样好，训练却快了大约5倍。

8d6b757cf810.en: Physical Intelligence's pi zero point five, in April 2025, asked what it takes to work in a home the robot has never seen. <bookmark mark='a'/> The model first writes a subtask in words, pick up the pillow, <bookmark mark='b'/> then the motion for it, with the flow-matching expert. <bookmark mark='c'/> And it is trained on everything at once: web data, many kinds of robot, and many different homes. In the company's own ablation, in unseen homes, the full model succeeded ninety-four percent of the time; without web data, seventy-four; without other robots' data, forty-nine; without the variety of homes, thirty-one. <bookmark mark='d'/> For robots, as for language, breadth of data is what generalizes.
8d6b757cf810.zh: Physical Intelligence在2025年4月推出的π0.5，问的是：要在一个机器人从没见过的家里干活，需要什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>模型先用文字写下一个子任务，比如捡起枕头，<bookmark mark='b'/>再用流匹配专家写出相应的动作。<bookmark mark='c'/>它同时在所有东西上训练：网络数据，许多种机器人，许多不同的家。在这家公司自己的消融实验里，在没见过的家中，完整的模型有94%的时候成功；去掉网络数据，74%；去掉其他机器人的数据，49%；去掉家庭的多样性，31%。<bookmark mark='d'/>对机器人和对语言一样，数据的广度才是泛化的来源。

75f0f0947d5c.en: Since then the field has moved fast, mostly through company reports. <bookmark mark='a'/> In March 2025 Google DeepMind built Gemini Robotics on its Gemini models, and NVIDIA released an open model for humanoids. <bookmark mark='b'/> In November Physical Intelligence added learning from experience: a value function scores how each moment is going, and the policy is told to act as the good moments did. It made espresso from five thirty in the morning to eleven thirty at night. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2026 came memory for tasks longer than ten minutes, <bookmark mark='d'/> and pi zero point seven, which can be prompted with the speed and quality wanted, or a picture of the next subgoal. <bookmark mark='e'/> This October, Google released a physical-reasoning model that plans and builds simulations, <bookmark mark='f'/> and Physical Intelligence opened its models to other robot makers. These are the companies' own results; independent benchmarks for robots are still young.
75f0f0947d5c.zh: 从那以后，这个领域进展飞快，主要是通过各家公司的报告。<bookmark mark='a'/>2025年3月，谷歌DeepMind在Gemini模型上建起了Gemini Robotics，英伟达发布了一个面向人形机器人的开放模型。<bookmark mark='b'/>同年11月，Physical Intelligence加入了从经验中学习：一个价值函数给每个时刻的进展打分，策略被告知要像那些好的时刻一样行动。它从早上五点半到晚上十一点半一直在做浓缩咖啡。<bookmark mark='c'/>2026年，出现了能做十分钟以上任务的记忆，<bookmark mark='d'/>还有π0.7，可以用想要的速度和质量来提示它，或者给它一张下一个子目标的图片。<bookmark mark='e'/>今年10月，谷歌发布了一个能做规划、能搭建仿真的物理推理模型，<bookmark mark='f'/>Physical Intelligence也把它的模型开放给了别的机器人厂商。这些都是公司自己的结果；面向机器人的独立基准，还很年轻。

e9ffdc092c4c.en: Let's take stock. An agent that cannot see everything acts on a belief, predicted and corrected by Bayes' rule. A language-model agent runs a loop of thoughts, actions and observations, with tools and memory around it. Over long tasks small errors compound, so reliability per step sets how far it can go, and on METR's measurements that reach has been doubling every few months. Copying an expert fails with the square of the horizon, and DAgger repairs it by learning where the learner actually goes. A world model lets an agent practise in its imagination, as our Dreamer did. And robots learn in randomized simulators and from demonstrations, with generative action experts and compressed action tokens.
e9ffdc092c4c.zh: 我们来盘点一下。一个看不全的智能体，依据信念行动，信念由贝叶斯法则不断预测和修正。语言模型智能体运行着一个由想法、动作和观测组成的循环，周围是工具和记忆。在长任务里，小错误会层层累积，所以每一步的可靠性，决定了它能走多远；按METR的测量，这个距离每隔几个月就翻一番。照搬专家，失败的程度随时程的平方增长；DAgger通过在学习者真正会去的地方学习来修复它。世界模型让智能体在想象中练习，我们的Dreamer就是这样做的。而机器人在随机化的仿真器里、从示范中学习，用的是生成式的动作专家和压缩过的动作词元。

26d24005aee2.en: All of this comes back. Whether the reasoning an agent writes is really how it decides, and whether networks carry models of their world inside them, are questions for Part 30. And how to evaluate agents, keep them from gaming their rewards, and control what they can touch, is the subject of the last part.
26d24005aee2.zh: 这一切都会再回来。智能体写下的推理，是不是它真正做决定的方式；网络内部是否带着它所在世界的模型：这些是第30部分的问题。而怎样评估智能体，怎样防止它们钻奖励的空子，怎样控制它们能碰什么，是最后一部分的主题。

8cc12672a3e2.en: Here are seven problems to try, from the belief update to the error of FAST's rounding. Pause here, and work through them; full solutions are in this part's notes.
8cc12672a3e2.zh: 这里有七道题可以试试，从信念更新，到FAST取整带来的误差。请在这里暂停，动手做一做；完整的解答在这一部分的笔记里。

6a3b7b970c97.en: Next time: inside the model. How a network stores more ideas than it has dimensions, <bookmark mark='a'/> how sparse autoencoders pull them apart, and how to trace a thought through its layers.
6a3b7b970c97.zh: 下一次：模型的内部。一个网络怎样存下比它的维数还多的概念，<bookmark mark='a'/>稀疏自编码器怎样把它们分开，以及怎样追踪一个想法穿过它的各层。

dd1e12c9a1eb.en: The best place to go deeper on the first half of this part is Thrun, Burgard and Fox's Probabilistic Robotics, and on learning to act, Sutton and Barto. Thanks for watching, and see you in Part 30.
dd1e12c9a1eb.zh: 想深入这一部分的前半，最好的去处是思伦、比尔加德和福克斯的《概率机器人》；想深入学习如何行动，是萨顿和巴托。感谢观看，第30部分见。
